name: ARC-GP: Anchored Residual Controller over the Gârleanu–Pedersen book (decision-aware Sharpe-after-cost residual, identity-initialised, capped, paired-tested against its own base)
mechanism:
DATA FLOW. Panel = true UTC daily OHLCV from the minute table (`trader/data.py:145-190` aggregate_asset_daily; `:319-345` load_db_backtest_panel include_dead=True), PIT membership via the present-mask (`trader/strategy.py:112`), liquidity filter as 819 (`trader/data.py:82`): T≈2,800 days × A≈273 assets, ~240–270 live per date. FORECAST LAYER (frozen, NOT learned here): the TASK_915 G-A cell(s) — ridge/GBM forecasts μ̂_{i,t,h} of the market-residual, Yang–Zhang-standardised forward return at h∈{1,3,7,21}d, refit quarterly, purge ≥h — plus σ̂_YZ, β̂ (90d), Σ̂ (Ledoit–Wolf on residuals), and signal decay φ_h from IC autocorrelation. BASE CONTROLLER w_GP: the GP closed form x_t=(1−a/λ)x_{t−1}+(a/λ)·aim_t, aim_t=(γΣ̂)^{-1}Σ_h μ̂_{t,h}/(1+φ_h a/γ), then a HARD β-neutral projection (Σ_i β̂_i x_i=0) and gross scaling to Σ|x|≤1 (spot, no leverage). This is a linear recurrence + projection: differentiable end to end, no QP layer needed. LEARNED OBJECT δ_θ: ONE small MLP shared across all assets and dates (≈20→64→64→3, ~5.5k params) with per-(i,t) inputs z_{i,t} = [μ̂_{i,t,h} ×4, w_GP,i,t, x_{i,t−1}, σ̂_YZ/σ̂_close-close ratio, Parkinson/GK ratio, range-to-close, dollar-volume rank, β̂, idio-vol, trailing 60d cross-sectional IC_h of the forecast ×4, date-level dispersion, market vol, N_present] plus a DeepSets date-context vector (mean/std of z over live assets). Three bounded outputs per asset, each a nameable channel: s_i∈[0,2] (forecast rescaling = state-dependent shrinkage; softplus), κ_i∈[0.25,4] (trading-rate multiplier on a/λ = the learned no-trade behaviour), δw_i∈[−c_i,c_i] with c_i=0.5|w_GP,i|+0.002 (additive position residual = cross-asset netting / nonlinear sizing; tanh). Book: w_t = Proj_β,gross( x_t^{GP}(s∘μ̂, κ·a/λ) + δw ). Residual-policy initialisation (Silver et al. 2018): s=1, κ=1, δw=0 exactly, so epoch 0 IS the GP book.

TARGETS AND LOSS (decision-aware; the realised return of the whole book is the label, there is no per-asset regression target): r^net_t = Σ_i w_{i,t−1} r_{i,t} − c·Σ_i |w_{i,t} − w̃_{i,t−1}| with c = 21 bp and w̃ the DRIFT-ADJUSTED previous weight (charges the re-trims the scorer's target-weight turnover misses — tactics-panel correction 3), simple returns (not the scorer's summed log returns — correction 2). L(θ) = −√365·mean(r^net)/std(r^net) [Zhang–Zohren–Roberts / Moody–Saffell batch Sharpe] + λ_a·mean[(log s)²+(log κ)²+(δw/c)²] (anchor to the GP identity, NOT to zero position) + λ_β·mean_t(Σ_i β̂_i w_{i,t})² + λ_g·mean_t relu(0.5 − Σ_i|w_{i,t}|)² (soft hold-positions floor). One training window = one sequence (turnover couples days), BPTT through the GP recurrence, Adam 1e-3, ≤300 epochs, early stopping on validation Sharpe. REFIT SCHEDULE: expanding-window walk-forward, folds of 6 months from 2021-H1 to 2026-H1 (≈11 folds); each fold trains on 2019-01→fold start minus a 21-day purge + 21-day embargo, validation = last 6 months of the training span (early stopping + λ_a∈{0.1,1,10} chosen HERE and only here), test = the 6 unseen months; 3 seeds (init) as replicates. CONTROL LAW at deployment: the frozen fold model maps today's z to (s,κ,δw); positions are target weights; EXECUTION RULE: daily at UTC close, target-weight rebalance, skip |Δw_i|<0.2% (RiskConfig band, `trader/config.py:128`), taker at 21 bp as the graded tier with a maker 8–12 bp arm as disclosed diagnostic. Grading through unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (position matrix in) AND `eval_vector.py --operator policy-argmax --vector-weight-rebalance` after ladder quantisation, agreement within 0.1 (882 two-instrument discipline). The deployable artifact = frozen forecasts + GP parameters + one 5.5k-param net + logged (s,κ,δw) per asset-day; setting s=κ=1, δw=0 recovers w_GP exactly.
math:
INPUTS (stated): bar +0.97 net@21 (survivor) / +0.56 (PIT), c = 21 bp/side on Σ|Δw| (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`, linear in turnover); σ_book ≈ 0.25/yr for a β-neutral $1-gross residual book (the directional 819 book is ≈0.60 — memo §1.4; check: its measured 0.155/day × 365 × 21 bp / 0.60 = 0.198 Sharpe of drag vs the measured 0.18 stack, `POWERED_RESULT.md:57` gross +0.74 → net@21 +0.56 — consistent); GP-book turnover τ ∈ [0.05, 0.10]/day (partial trading at rate a/λ; 915 measures it); N_eff ∈ {5, 8, 15} (participation ratio, unmeasured, TASK_825 parked); TC ≈ 0.6 (cost-aware controller); daily decisions, √365.
COST DRAG in Sharpe units = τ·365·c/σ_book: τ=0.05 → 0.153; 0.08 → 0.245; 0.10 → 0.307. Note the perverse direction: a market-neutral book has LOWER σ so the same turnover costs MORE Sharpe than on the 819 book.
GROSS IR REQUIRED = bar + drag: for +0.97: 1.12 / 1.22 / 1.28; for +0.56: 0.71 / 0.81 / 0.87 (τ = 0.05/0.08/0.10).
FUNDAMENTAL LAW IR = IC·√(365·N_eff)·TC ⇒ IC_needed = IR/(√(365·N_eff)·TC). At τ=0.08, TC=0.6: N_eff=8 (√BR=54.0): IC 0.038 for +0.97, 0.025 for +0.56; N_eff=15 (74.0): 0.027 / 0.018; N_eff=5 (42.7): 0.048 / 0.032. At exactly G-A's floor (IC=0.02, N_eff=8): gross 0.65, net ≈ +0.40 at τ=0.08 — below both bars; δ would have to add +0.57.
WHAT δ CAN ADD, channel by channel (bounds, not hopes): (1) cost channel ≤ the drag itself (0.15–0.31); realistic recovery 20–40% of it by learned no-trade behaviour → +0.05..+0.10 (Lim et al. 2019 Exhibit 8: cost-in-loss lifts a Sharpe-loss LSTM from −5.31 to +0.91 at 10 bp — to benchmark parity +0.86, not above it). (2) variance channel: Sharpe ∝ 1/σ at fixed mean; a 10–15% σ reduction from state-conditioned gross → +8–17% of gross ≈ +0.05..+0.15 (Cederburg et al. 2020 via tactics panel: 8/103 strategies, MOM the outlier). (3) calibration channel: TC 0.6 → 0.75 via state-dependent shrinkage of unreliable forecasts → +25% of gross ≈ +0.15..+0.25 at gross 0.65–1.0 — the largest, but it re-uses the SAME first moment, so it is bounded by the IC ceiling, never above it. TOTAL plausible +0.15..+0.35, expected +0.10..+0.20. ADMISSION RULE derived from this: run δ only if the 915 G-C GP book reads ≥ +0.60 net@21 on 2024-01→2026-06 (required Δ ≤ +0.37, inside the plausible band); at a GP read of +0.40 the row is not worth building.
GP BASE (Gârleanu–Pedersen 2013, Λ=λΣ): x_t=(1−a/λ)x_{t−1}+(a/λ)aim_t; a=[−(γ(1−ρ)+λρ)+√((γ(1−ρ)+λρ)²+4γλ(1−ρ)²)]/(2(1−ρ)); aim_t=(γΣ)^{-1}Σ_h μ̂_h/(1+φ_h a/γ) — slower-decaying horizons weighted more. λ calibration: match ½λσ_d²d² = c·d at a representative trade d=0.5% of book: λ = 2c/(σ_d²·d); for an 80%-vol asset σ_d²=0.8²/365=0.00175 → λ ≈ 2·0.0021/(0.00175·0.005) ≈ 480. The quadratic proxy equals the repo's LINEAR cost at exactly one trade size and mis-prices all others (Constantinides/Davis–Norman: the ℓ1-optimal rule is a no-trade band, width ∝ (c/γσ²)^{1/3}) — this is the misspecification the κ channel targets, and the ℓ1-MPC control arm (Boyd et al. 2017) must be beaten before learning is credited.
LOSS: L(θ) = −√365·mean(r^net)/std(r^net) + λ_a·mean[(log s)²+(log κ)²+(δw/c)²] + λ_β·mean_t(Σ_iβ̂_i w_{i,t})² + λ_g·mean_t relu(0.5−Σ|w|)²; r^net_t = Σ_i w_{i,t−1}r_{i,t} − c·Σ_i|w_{i,t}−w̃_{i,t−1}|.
MULTIPLICITY: SR0(N) = E[max_N SR|H0] ≈ σ_SR·[(1−γ)Z(1−1/N)+γZ(1−1/(N·e))], σ_SR≈1/√T_yrs = 0.632 on the 2.5-yr goalpost window (Bailey–López de Prado form; γ≈0.577): N=1 → 0; N=3 → 0.54; N=10 → 0.97 (reproduces the loops panel's "clears +0.97 at N≈10"); N=27 (3 seeds × 3 λ_a × 3 architectures) → 1.26. Hence the TEST read is N=1: one pre-registered architecture, λ_a fixed on validation, seeds are replicates (median), and SR0(N_val) is printed beside the validation choice.
POWER OF THE PAIRED TEST (the honest part): with |δw| ≤ 0.5|w_GP| the difference series r_{GP+δ}−r_GP has σ_Δ ≲ 0.4·σ_book ⇒ SE(Δ_SR) ≈ 0.4/√T = 0.25 on 2.5 yr, 0.17 on the 5.5-yr walk-forward span. A true Δ=+0.20 is a 0.8σ / 1.2σ event. The pre-registered read will most likely return a WIDE NULL on the goalpost window — as 892's calibration predicted for its own 116-decision leg — and NULL is scored as FAIL (δ deleted). Primary paired read therefore = full walk-forward span 2021-H1→2026-H1 (≈11 folds); the 2024–26 slice is the goalpost read, not the power read.
profit_source: FORECAST — of the market-residual, vol-standardised conditional mean of forward returns at h∈{1,3,7,21}d — and ONLY through the frozen TASK_915 forecasts; δ adds NO first-moment information (by the iterated-expectations identity E[gross]=Σ_t E[w_t·E[r_{t+1}|F_t]], loops panel). δ's own contribution is attributed to two secondary sources, each isolated by an ablation arm: (i) COST REDUCTION — the κ channel learns state-dependent no-trade behaviour that the quadratic GP proxy cannot express under the repo's linear cost, bounded above by the measured drag (0.15–0.31 Sharpe at τ 0.05–0.10/day, σ_book 0.25); (ii) the Sharpe-DENOMINATOR (variance) via the s and δw channels — conditioning gross and cross-asset netting on range-based vol state (Yang–Zhang/Parkinson/GK ratios, dispersion) and on forecast reliability (trailing cross-sectional IC). No risk premium and no rebalancing premium is claimed: the scorer sums constituent log returns and cannot see one (`trader/backtest.py:221-223`, tactics-panel correction 2), and the book is β-neutral by hard projection so it carries no market premium in either direction.
why_learning: A closed-form estimator uses each piece of second-moment/state information through one scalar: GP shrinks all forecasts by one λ and one γ, sizes linearly in μ̂, prices every trade quadratically, and treats Σ̂ and φ_h as known. The map from (μ̂ at four horizons, trailing forecast reliability, range-based vol state, dispersion, current position, cost) to the position ADJUSTMENT is a nonlinear function of ~20 inputs with interactions — forecast × reliability × cost is the one that decides whether a re-trim is worth 21 bp — and no closed form has it; a Bayesian shrinkage by trailing IC gets one interaction, a no-trade band gets another, an ℓ1-MPC gets a third, none gets them jointly. Three properties make LEARNING the efficient estimator here rather than a luxury: (1) parameter sharing — one 5.5k-parameter net over 273 assets × ~2,000 training days ≈ 550k asset-days for a sizing map that is plausibly the same function for every asset (the inputs are already vol- and cross-sectionally standardised), whereas per-asset closed-form calibration has ~2,000 points each; (2) the decision-aware loss — training on the realised Sharpe-after-cost of the book is the only objective that scores the four misspecifications (quadratic-vs-linear cost, Gaussian sizing under fat tails, Σ̂ error, φ̂_h error) jointly in the currency the goalposts use; Elmachtoub–Grigas prove the SPO+ surrogate is Fisher-consistent and report that decision losses dominate two-stage fitting precisely when the model is misspecified, and Butler–Kwon measure it on 24 commodity futures 2000–2020: integrated (IPO) Sharpe 0.759 vs two-stage OLS 0.374, gross of costs; (3) the anchor — because δ is initialised at the GP identity and penalised toward it, the learned object is only the CORRECTION, so with no information the estimator returns the closed form rather than noise (Silver et al. 2018 residual policy learning: the base controller supplies the structure, the network the residual). Honest limit: the information δ exploits beyond GP is second-moment and state information; the 819 CAPACITY read (MLP OOS IC +0.0358 vs ridge −0.0104 at H=1, inside a ±0.059 four-draw noise band, `CAPACITY_RESULT.md`) is inconclusive about nonlinear FORECASTING and says nothing about nonlinear SIZING, which no row has measured.

bear_positive.argument: The book is β-neutral by HARD projection (Σβ̂_i w_i = 0 enforced after δ, not learned), so its expected return in BEAR22 equals the residual alpha harvested in 2022 — positive iff the TASK_915 G-A cell's cross-sectional IC is > 0 in 2022 (915 reports IC by year; 2022 is in-window for the form check, 2026H1 is the unseen bear-ish read). δ cannot manufacture a bear premium; it can only preserve or destroy the residual one. The known destruction mode is vol-conditioning: the 819 book earned most in its highest-vol regime (BEAR22 net@21 +1.06 PIT, `POWERED_RESULT.md:54`), so a gross-throttling s/κ channel trained on calm years would cut exposure exactly where a residual book earns (Cederburg et al.'s caution); guard = 2022 is always inside the training window for every fold that grades 2024–26, and the pre-registered gates require BEAR22 net@21 > 0 for w_GP+δ AND Δ(BEAR22) ≥ −0.1 vs w_GP. Unmodelled: spot-margin borrow cost on the short leg (~50% of gross in a β-neutral book), which the record has never priced; a positive BEAR22 read is conditional on that too.

guards: 887 ADAPTIVE HOLD COLLAPSE — structurally unreachable, not merely discouraged: the base is a closed-form book on an external forecast (flat only if μ̂≈0, which is 915's job to rule out), δ is anchored to the GP IDENTITY (s=κ=1, δw=0), not to zero position, and the cap |δw_i| ≤ 0.5|w_GP,i|+0.002 plus κ ≥ 0.25 means δ cannot flatten more than half the book on any day; the 887 fixed point — 'my actions have negative EV, so do nothing' — has no cost-free HOLD action to retreat to because turnover is priced INSIDE the loss and the anchor is priced too. Pre-registered FAIL: median gross(w) < 0.5·median gross(w_GP), or > 5% of test days with gross < 0.1, or median s < 0.5 with κ < 0.5 (the visible form of the collapse, logged per asset-day). 892 RE-TRIM DAMAGE — the anti-edge lived in maintenance re-trims of an imprint trained with no cost in its targets (Δ −0.060/−0.062/−0.050, every CI < 0; entries/exits NULL). Here (a) the loss charges every re-trim at 21 bp with DRIFT-INCLUSIVE accounting so δ cannot exploit the scorer's uncharged drift re-trims (+9–12×/yr ≈ −0.03..−0.04 Sharpe, tactics-panel correction 3); (b) κ ≤ 4 bounds turnover to ≤ 4× GP's; (c) the evaluation decomposes Δ into entries/exits vs maintenance re-trims exactly as 892's co-primary did — a negative re-trim component with CI excluding 0 deletes δ regardless of the headline. 813 SELECTION LUCK (132 cells → 1 'GO' on n=6 events → 0/48 on hold-out, `runs/813_volharvest/PHASE1_5_RESULT.md`) — N_test = 1: one pre-registered architecture and λ_a grid {0.1,1,10} resolved on the validation slice inside the training span; seeds are replicates (median reported with spread), never choices; the test read is a single paired number per fold. MULTIPLICITY SR0(N) reported beside every selection: SR0(N) = 0.632·[(1−γ)Z(1−1/N)+γZ(1−1/(Ne))] on 2.5 yr → N=3: 0.54, N=10: 0.97, N=27: 1.26; the validation grid's SR0(9) ≈ 0.94 is printed next to the chosen λ_a so the reader sees that validation Sharpe alone is not evidence. PLACEBO: 20 trainings on circularly shifted returns (shift ≥ 63 d) give the null distribution of Δ under 'learning on noise with this many parameters and this anchor'; PASS needs Δ_real > its 95th percentile; a block-Rademacher sign-flip null on the paired Δ series (loops-panel surviving item) is the second null. CLOSED-FORM COMPETITOR: an ℓ1-cost MPC arm (Boyd et al.) with plug-in parameters runs beside δ; if it matches δ within the paired CI, learning is deleted and the MPC stands — learning must beat the best closed form, not just GP. INSTRUMENT: unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (seed 819, n_boot 2000) for absolute numbers; the 892 calibrated-width block-bootstrap interval for the paired Δ (block 21, coverage 0.940–0.975 certified); `eval_vector` agreement within 0.1.

why_not_falsified.receipt: LEDGER 887/collapse-confirm (A −2.855% / E −9.106% / D −13.844% at hold 99.0/95.7/91.2%, fee 0) and 884/885: the collapse is the distillation loop's fixed point, search depth irrelevant
why_not_falsified.argument: Those loops had no external forecast, a free HOLD action, and targets that were their own visit distribution; the adaptive collapse was the correct response to a negative-EV action set. ARC-GP has no self-generated targets (the label is realised book return), no free HOLD (turnover and the anchor are both in the loss), and a base that is non-flat by construction whenever 915's forecast is non-zero. The 887 attractor is not on the reachable set (|δw| ≤ 0.5|w_GP|, κ ≥ 0.25).

why_not_falsified.receipt: LEDGER 892/action-ev: Δ −0.0503/−0.0559/−0.0428 OOS, anti-edge concentrated in maintenance re-trims (−0.060/−0.062/−0.050), entries/exits NULL; D47
why_not_falsified.argument: 892 audited BC-imprinted argmax policies whose training targets carried no cost and whose re-trims were therefore unpriced. ARC-GP prices every re-trim inside the loss with drift-inclusive accounting and makes the 892 decomposition a gate. The record shows WHERE a learned book fails OOS; this design puts the cost of that exact behaviour into the gradient.

why_not_falsified.receipt: LEDGER 875/wf-generalization (1/5 folds; OOS median flat +0.31/+0.40/+0.41 while the floor swung 15×; f5 −2.9566), 861/ref-rebase (+0.9914 in-window, seed spread 0.041), 879 (search Δ 1.602 subtractive)
why_not_falsified.argument: All three are the 832 imprint recipe (BC on hard argmax targets) with or without the search wrapper — a policy that fused forecast and control. Here the forecast is a frozen supervised object graded separately (915) and the learned part is a bounded correction to a closed-form controller; 875's finding that the policy 'does not track window difficulty' is exactly what the anchor prevents: when the forecast is weak, δ returns the GP book, which tracks it by construction.

why_not_falsified.receipt: runs/819_single_asset/PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:70 tanh-continuous sizing +0.88 vs sign +0.97 net@21 (−0.09); lever attribution invvol −0.06, lookback ensemble −0.16
why_not_falsified.argument: These are single-scalar, hand-set sizing rules on the trend signal, each a knob; none conditions on forecast reliability, range-based vol state or cost, and none was fitted to the realised after-cost Sharpe. They bound what a scalar rule does (≈ −0.1..0); they do not measure a learned state-dependent map. They DO lower the prior on channel (2): the record's every hand sizing tweak read ≤ 0.

why_not_falsified.receipt: Lim–Zohren–Roberts 2019 §VI (full text): Sharpe-loss LSTM trades ≈10× the Long-Only benchmark's turnover, outperforms only to 2–3 bp; at c=10 bp LSTM −5.313 vs LSTM+turnover-regulariser +0.912 vs Sgn(Returns) +0.861
why_not_falsified.argument: The DMN failure at 21 bp (tactics panel: dead) is a FROM-SCRATCH Sharpe-loss policy with unbounded turnover; the same paper shows that cost-in-loss restores benchmark parity. ARC-GP starts AT the cost-aware benchmark (GP), bounds turnover to ≤ 4× it, and grades only the paired increment — the DMN failure mode is designed out. The same bound caps the upside, which is why the odds below are low.

controllability: High, by construction, and this is the main thing the design buys over the 828 line. (1) Three named channels with logged values per asset-day — s (forecast scale), κ (trading-rate multiplier), δw (position residual) — each mapping to one profit source (calibration / cost / variance), each individually ablatable and individually deletable if its paired contribution is ≤ 0. (2) Hard bounds the operator sets, not learns: |δw| ≤ 0.5|w_GP|+0.002, κ∈[0.25,4], s∈[0,2], β-neutrality and Σ|w|≤1 by projection; λ_a sets the maximum plausible deviation from the closed form and is the only tuned scalar. (3) Kill switch with zero retraining: s=κ=1, δw=0 recovers the GP book bit-for-bit; the deployable artifact is frozen forecasts + GP parameters + a 5.5k-parameter net + a position matrix, gradable by the unmodified `trader/` scorer — a bill of materials, not a checkpoint whose behaviour has to be inferred from rollouts. (4) Flat is visible: 887's attractor becomes a logged (s→0, κ→small) pattern with a pre-registered FAIL band, not a silent argmax. (5) The failure surfaces the record names (re-trim damage, gross collapse, turnover inflation) each have a pre-registered numeric gate, and the closed-form ℓ1-MPC arm gives the operator a non-learned fallback of equal auditability if δ is deleted.
compute: Small; CPU-feasible; one 24 GB card is more than enough and 64 GB cards are irrelevant. Panel float32 2,800×273×20 features ≈ 61 MB. Per epoch: MLP 20→64→64→3 (~5.5k params) over 2,800×273 asset-days ≈ 4.6 GFLOP forward, ≈15 GFLOP with backward; GP recurrence 2,800 dense 273×273 mat-vecs ≈ 0.2 GFLOP; BPTT over T≈2,000 steps holds ~2,000×273×64 activations ≈ 140 MB. Full protocol: 11 folds × 3 seeds × 3 λ_a × ≤300 epochs ≈ 30k epochs ≈ 4.5e14 FLOP → ~1 GPU-hour on one 3090 at modest utilisation, or a few CPU-hours; plus 20 placebo trainings (~+60%) and the ℓ1-MPC arm (a 273-variable QP per day, cvxpy/OSQP, seconds per fold). Everything runs safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server per `.claude/rules/10-compute-allocation.md`; no self-play, no world model, no tree. The scoring side is `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (CPU, minutes) and one `eval_vector` pass per fold for the two-instrument check. Build effort ≈ 2–3 agent-days on top of TASK_915's forecast and GP artifacts, which are prerequisites, not part of this row.

kill_experiment.design: PRECONDITION (hard): TASK_915 G-A PASS and the G-C GP book graded, with W_GP frozen as a position matrix on the PIT panel; ADMISSION: GP net@21 ≥ +0.60 on 2024-01→2026-06 (else the row is not built — required Δ would exceed δ's bounded range). ARMS, all on the identical panel/forecasts/scorer: (0) W_GP frozen; (1) W_GP+δ — ONE pre-registered architecture (20→64→64→3, caps as stated), λ_a∈{0.1,1,10} and early-stopping epoch chosen on the validation slice inside each fold's training span, 3 seeds as replicates, expanding-window walk-forward 2021-H1→2026-H1 (≈11 six-month folds, 21 d purge + 21 d embargo); (2) placebo: 20 δ trainings on circularly shifted returns (shift ≥ 63 d), same protocol; (3) ℓ1-MPC control (Boyd et al.) with plug-in parameters, no learning; (4) channel ablations s-only / κ-only / δw-only (reported for attribution, not gates). Every gate below is fixed in the SPEC before the first fit (sha256 recorded); the cell grid is closed; a second architecture is a new row.
kill_experiment.instrument: Absolute numbers: unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (seed 819, n_boot 2000, tiers 8/21, simple-return series alongside the log-return default). Paired Δ: daily r_{GP+δ}−r_GP with the 892 calibrated-width block bootstrap (block 21; CALIBRATION_TABLE coverage 0.940–0.975) and a block-Rademacher sign-flip null; 892-style decomposition of Δ into entries/exits vs maintenance re-trims (drift-inclusive turnover). Two-instrument check: `eval_vector.py --operator policy-argmax --vector-weight-rebalance` on the ladder-quantised W_GP+δ, agreement within 0.1 (882 discipline). Multiplicity: SR0(N_val) printed beside the chosen λ_a; N_test = 1. Epoch and PIT frame pinned per LEDGER.md:28-41.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: PASS requires ALL of: (i) seed-median paired Δ net@21 over the full walk-forward span > 0 with calibrated CI lo > 0 on ≥ 2/3 seeds; (ii) on the goalpost window 2024-01→2026-06, W_GP+δ net@21 ≥ +0.97 with bootstrap CI lo > 0 (record MARGINAL if ≥ +0.56 with (i) holding); (iii) Δ_real > 95th percentile of the 20 placebo Δs; (iv) Δ vs the ℓ1-MPC arm > 0 with CI lo > 0 (else the MPC stands and δ is deleted — learning must beat the best closed form); (v) hold-positions: median gross(W_GP+δ) ≥ 0.5·median gross(W_GP), ≤ 5% of days with gross < 0.1; (vi) BEAR22 net@21 > 0 for W_GP+δ and Δ(BEAR22) ≥ −0.1; 2026H1 net@21 > 0; (vii) the maintenance-re-trim component of Δ is not negative with CI excluding 0; (viii) turnover(W_GP+δ) ≤ 1.5× turnover(W_GP), or Δ survives re-grading at 30 bp. FAIL on any one → δ is deleted, the GP (or MPC) book stands, and the row records the channel ablations so the record knows WHICH channel failed. A WIDE NULL on (i) is scored FAIL and is the pre-registered most-likely outcome given SE(Δ_SR) ≈ 0.17–0.25.
kill_experiment.cost: CPU: a few hours (or ≤ 1 GPU-hour) for training + placebos + MPC arm; scoring minutes. Build 2–3 agent-days on top of TASK_915's artifacts. Kill date 10 days from SPEC commit, gated behind 915 G-C. No GPU-days, no server training queue.

honest_odds: Chain, stated so it can be scored. P(915 G-A passes: IC ≥ 0.02, NW t ≥ 3 after Bonferroni, positive in each of 2024/2025/2026H1) ≈ 30% (slightly above the memo's P(clears +0.56) ≈ 25%, since G-A is a weaker event). P(G-C GP book reads ≥ +0.60 net@21 on 2024–26H1 | G-A) ≈ 50% — this is the admission gate; below it the row is not built. P(δ adds a paired Δ ≥ +0.10 with CI excluding 0 on the walk-forward span | admitted) ≈ 30–35%: the literature's end-to-end gains are real but small and cost-fragile (Zhang et al. +0.38 → +0.10 as cost goes 1 → 10 bp; Lim et al. cost-in-loss reaches parity, not above; Butler–Kwon's 2× is gross of costs on futures), the repo's every hand-sizing tweak read ≤ 0 (−0.06/−0.09/−0.16), and the paired test is under-powered for the plausible effect. P(W_GP+δ ≥ +0.97 with CI lo > 0 | G-A) ≈ 12–15%; the increment over what GP alone would already achieve (the event that JUSTIFIES the learned part) ≈ 6–8% conditional on G-A. UNCONDITIONAL: P(goalposts) ≈ 4%; P(δ is the reason) ≈ 2%. If G-A fails, this mechanism is exactly the memo's near-flat book with a decoration on it — zero, by construction, and the pre-committed D79 consequence (data row, not model row) applies with nothing here to argue against it. What the row buys even on FAIL: the first measurement of nonlinear cost-aware SIZING on a fixed forecast, the ℓ1-MPC vs quadratic-GP comparison, and a channel attribution — all closed-form-comparable, none of which the record has.
open_doubts: Everything is downstream of TASK_915 G-A. If the daily residual conditional mean is ≈ 0 on 2024–26, the identity E[gross] = Σ_t E[w_t·E[r_{t+1}|F_t]] makes ARC-GP's expected gross zero for any θ and its net −turnover × 21 bp; the anchor then returns the GP book, which is itself near-flat. The mechanism has no independent alpha claim and should not be scheduled before 915 reports.

Power. With |δw| ≤ 0.5|w_GP| the paired Δ series has SE(Δ_SR) ≈ 0.25 on the 2.5-yr goalpost window and ≈ 0.17 on the 5.5-yr walk-forward span; the plausible effect (+0.10..+0.20) is a ~1σ event. The pre-registered rule scores NULL as FAIL, so a genuinely useful δ of +0.15 will most likely be deleted — the conservative error, but an error. Loosening the cap to raise σ_Δ raises power and simultaneously re-opens the 887/892 surface; I do not see a clean resolution.

The gradient of a batch Sharpe over ~2,000 daily portfolio returns with N_eff ≈ 8 carries roughly 2,000 effective observations for a 5.5k-parameter net; the anchor is doing most of the statistical work and the 'learning' may reduce in practice to a data-driven shrinkage toward GP. If the ablations show the s-channel (a near-scalar shrinkage) carries all of Δ, the honest conclusion is that a closed-form Bayesian shrinkage by trailing IC should replace the net.

The quadratic GP proxy vs the repo's linear cost is a real misspecification, but its natural fix is the ℓ1-MPC (Boyd et al.) or a Davis–Norman band — no learning needed. The design includes MPC as a control arm for exactly this reason; a plausible outcome is 'MPC ≥ δ', which ends the learned part and leaves a closed-form controller improvement — worth having, but not the operator's question.

Non-stationarity of the sizing map: the vol-state → gross relation learned on 2019–2023 may not hold in 2024–26 (loops panel: detection windows for IC 0.02–0.03 exceed regime lifetimes). Quarterly refits mitigate; they also add re-trims that the loss must price.

Borrow cost and short availability on Kraken spot margin are unmodelled for a book whose short gross is ~50%; the record has never priced them, and BEAR-positivity of a β-neutral book depends on the short leg being executable at the assumed cost.

The operator's actual Kraken fee tier is unrecorded (loops panel: no tier has a 16 bp maker or taker); every 21 bp number here — and the cost-channel's entire upside — moves with it. Writing the tier down is a zero-cost prerequisite to interpreting the cost channel.

Two-instrument agreement: `eval_vector`'s ±w_unit ladder quantises small δw adjustments to zero; if the two instruments disagree by > 0.1 the disagreement is most likely the ladder, not a defect, but the 882 discipline says the row is not a result until it is resolved — this should be pre-registered as a named residual, not left to be argued after the fact.

The scorer's turnover charges target-weight changes only (backtest.py:224-227) and sums log returns (221-223); the loss uses drift-inclusive turnover and simple returns. The two will disagree slightly by construction; the SPEC must state which is the graded number (the unmodified scorer, per the goalposts) and report the other as a disclosed diagnostic.
